evidence_level: Posthoc explanatory diagnostics on existing F128 seed0 frozen natural ColNomic C128 results, fixed threshold zero; no new training, jobs, token-cache forward passes, or official score changes.

native_operator.pair: delta(g,r)=0.5*(ordered(g,r)-ordered(r,g)); ordered comparison uses aligned native query tokens before mean/attention pooling.
native_operator.rivals: Let a=RAW, b=highest frozen B_CAL nonanchor, c=second. For g outside {a,b}, rivals={a,b}; for b, rivals={a,c}; for a, rivals={b}. Immutable physical row ascending resolves baseline-score ties.
native_operator.pool: Dg=mean(valid pair edges), logits_g=base_g+Dg-Da, logit_a=0; strict unique-best challenger >0 SWITCH, otherwise HOLD.

structural_derivation.transitive_assumption: Suppose delta(g,r)=f(g)-f(r), which QR satisfies by construction but QRR is not required to satisfy.
structural_derivation.g_vs_b: For g outside {a,b}, Dg-Db=f(g)-f(b)-0.5*(f(b)-f(c)). Thus differing opponents can alter ranks even with exactly transitive pair scores.
structural_derivation.common_opponents: Using exactly {a,b} for every candidate, retaining self pair zero and denominator 2, gives Dg-Da=f(g)-f(a) under transitivity.
structural_derivation.exact_observed_native_minus_common_g_vs_: -0.5*delta(b,c) for g outside {a,b}, without needing transitivity; values -1.2980490019062305 and -1.4849171761974524 for the two losses.

findings: Loss 1 (H593-1af45..., fold0): same MULTI weights RAW-only and common-opponent probes both switch to correct physical1183; native selects wrong1980. Native margin -0.743059 becomes +0.849198 or +0.554990. Therefore the native aggregation operator is sufficient to flip this fixed-model decision from correct to wrong.

Loss 2 (H593-2e515..., fold4): native margin -1.584615 improves to -0.461516 RAW-only and -0.099698 common-opponents, but both still select wrong1966. The native operator contributes harm; removing it alone is insufficient. Separate trained ANCHOR margin is only +0.004075 and its selected epoch6 differs from MULTI epoch4. These are trained-model/selection differences, not an isolated operator effect.

Both targets have positive direct pair evidence versus their wrong b (2.072793 and1.687169), while b-vs-c edges (2.596098 and2.969834) are stronger. Mixing incomparable opponents reduces target-vs-b residual margin; on loss2 it reverses that residual margin from +0.963534 to -0.159566.

The subtraction of RAW D increases target-vs-RAW logits in both cases: +0.952993 and+2.457913 relative to RAW-only; it is a common shift among nonanchors and cancels from target-vs-wrong-nonanchor margins. Saying the target score simply decreased would be false.

Across all128, each fixed probe yields107 correct versus native106, with2 rescues and1 break,5 decision changes. The lost previously correct query is H593-17e572..., so this is not a free improvement or validated replacement.

16,128 native MULTI triangles show nontransitivity (RMS cycle/edge26.44%). The two loss target cycles have opposite signs and nontransitivity respectively harms and helps their g-vs-b margins. It cannot alone explain both losses.
limits: M0 stays byte-equal to frozen common features; local mean_v remains a scalar cache channel. The reader adds learned local content/support use without recomputing that global coverage scalar.
MULTI is RAW plus one baseline-chosen rival per candidate, with candidate-dependent opponent sets and unweighted mean; it is not full all-pairs competition.
Extra information can improve pair decisions yet harm ranking when opponent sets differ; the evidence here is restricted to the fixed saved-edge interventions.
No external test, no renewed OOF model selection, no claim that either posthoc107 score is an official benchmark result.
rerun: Keep probe_saved_edges.py and portable_input_snapshot.json in the same directory; run python probe_saved_edges.py using Python3.9+. Default replay uses only stdlib and this snapshot. --from-originals revalidates original bound workspace artifacts and regenerates snapshot.
